verdicts.claim: arSession is a read-only handle; RoomPlan installs its own ARSessionDelegate on it and manages the ARWorldTrackingConfiguration. Replacing arSession.delegate breaks the scan (camera preview goes black / SLAM never initializes). To receive ARFrames alongside RoomPlan, either (a) chain: capture the existing arSession.delegate after run() and forward to it from your own delegate (delegate multiplexer), or (b) attach an ARSCNView/ARView to the session and use ARSCNViewDelegate renderer callbacks, which are independent of ARSession.delegate. Reading arSession.currentFrame (pose, capturedImage, camera intrinsics) is fine.
verdicts.correction: Rely on: `var arSession: ARSession` on RoomCaptureSession (iOS 16.0+, set by RoomPlan at init, read-only); `init(arSession: ARSession? = nil)` (iOS 17.0+); `stop(pauseARSession: Bool = true)` (iOS 17.0+); `RoomCaptureView(frame:arSession:)` (iOS 17.0+). ARSession.delegate is declared `weak var delegate: (any ARSessionDelegate)? { get set }` (iOS 11.0+), a single weak slot, so whoever assigns last wins and the owner must retain the delegate object. No Apple document says RoomPlan installs its own ARSessionDelegate, and shipped code (facebookresearch/ocean) creates RoomCaptureSession(), calls run(configuration:), then sets arSession.delegate = self and still implements all RoomCaptureSessionDelegate callbacks, so the claim that replacing the delegate breaks the scan is not supported. Mapper pattern: create its own ARSession, set arSession.delegate (retain the delegate object strongly elsewhere) and optionally delegateQueue BEFORE handing the session to RoomCaptureSession(arSession:), then run(configuration:). Keep a cheap defensive multiplexer only if a device log shows RoomPlan replaced the delegate (check `session.delegate === self` after captureSession(_:didStartWith:)). Parts of the verifier's correction I reject: the article does NOT show any code that sets arSession.delegate, and it does NOT prove the app must be ARSession.delegate. It only says the code 'implements an ARSessionObserver'; ARSessionObserver is also the parent protocol of ARSCNViewDelegate (`protocol ARSCNViewDelegate : ARSessionObserver, SCNSceneRendererDelegate`), so those callbacks can equally arrive through an ARSCNView delegate. Also, in the article the relocalization happens on the app's own session ('relocalizedARSession') BEFORE `RoomCaptureSession(arSession:relocalizedARSession)` is created, so it says nothing about delegate ownership during an active RoomPlan scan. Option (b) of the claim (ARSCNViewDelegate/ARSessionObserver via a view) is therefore a valid alternative, just not required.
verdicts.reasoning: Ruling on the reality verdict: the verifier is right that the 'RoomPlan owns the delegate and overriding breaks SLAM' premise is unsupported, but overstated the article. Fresh fetch of scanning-the-rooms-of-a-single-structure.json: its code listings are `RoomCaptureSession()`, `RoomCaptureView(frame:arSession:)`, `run(configuration:)`, `stop(pauseARSession:false)`, a didEndWith handler, `func sessionShouldAttemptRelocalization(_ session: ARSession) -> Bool { return true }`, `func session(_ session: ARSession, cameraDidChangeTrackingState camera: ARCamera)` and `RoomCaptureSession(arSession:relocalizedARSession)`; the prose says 'the following code implements an ARSessionObserver'. There is no `delegate =` assignment anywhere, so the article names no object as ARSession delegate. arkit/arsession/delegate.json: `weak var delegate: (any ARSessionDelegate)? { get set }`, iOS 11.0, single slot. arkit/arscnviewdelegate.json: ARSCNViewDelegate inherits ARSessionObserver, so the article's observer callbacks do not strictly require being ARSession.delegate. roomcapturesession/arsession.json: iOS 16.0, 'RoomCaptureSession sets this property at initialization and throws an error if your app attempts to set a value' (this is about the arSession property itself, not its delegate). Re-read facebookresearch/ocean AKRoomPlanTracker6DOF_Swift.swift via raw.githubusercontent.com: order is RoomCaptureSession(), run(configuration:), then arSession.delegate = self; it implements session(_:didUpdate:) plus didStartWith/didAdd/didRemove/didChange/didUpdate/didProvide/didEndWith, i.e. room callbacks are expected to keep flowing after the override. Apple forum thread 710134 (DTS-answered) shows developers accessing arSession for depth without any mention of a RoomPlan-internal delegate. The two refuted/refuting positions are reconciled as: setting arSession.delegate is allowed and is the standard way to get ARFrames; the ARSCNView route also works; a multiplexer is optional. Runtime confirmation on iOS 18.3.2 is still a device test (see open questions).

open_question_answers.question: Does RoomPlan on iOS 18.3 preserve sceneReconstruction / sceneDepth on a custom ARSession that was run with them before RoomCaptureSession.run? (Community says yes with pre-run or re-run after didStartWith; a Dec 2025 report says depth stays nil.) Needs one device test.
open_question_answers.answer: Likely no for a bare RoomCaptureSession: the configuration is replaced when run(configuration:) is called, so re-apply it. Docs lean yes (WWDC23 10192: a custom ARSession is 'honored'; RoomCaptureView(frame:arSession:) says RoomPlan preserves the AR session's settings, but that sentence is scoped to the view initializer). Field reports on the headless RoomCaptureSession path say otherwise: Apple forum thread 763400 (Sep 2024) reports sceneDepth disappears from ARFrames once RoomCaptureSession runs on a custom session, and its accepted answer is to re-run a sceneDepth-enabled ARWorldTrackingConfiguration after captureSession(_:didStartWith:) fires; threads 808834 (Dec 2025) and 728601 agree (728601 reports the RoomCaptureView path behaves differently). Thread 710134's accepted 'fix' compares to nil and proves nothing. Mapper design (consistent with the arkit-mesh-depth tie-breaker): build ARWorldTrackingConfiguration with sceneReconstruction .meshWithClassification and frameSemantics [.sceneDepth] (check supportsFrameSemantics / supportsSceneReconstruction), run it on Mapper's own ARSession, pass it to RoomCaptureSession(arSession:), call run(configuration:), then inside captureSession(_:didStartWith:) call arSession.run(config) with NO options (no .resetTracking / .removeExistingAnchors, which keeps tracking and anchors), repeat for every room, and keep a watchdog that re-applies when frame.sceneDepth is nil. Device test: log once per second during a RoomPlan scan session.configuration?.frameSemantics.contains(.sceneDepth), videoFormat, frame.sceneDepth != nil, and the ARMeshAnchor count, before and after the re-apply, and confirm CapturedRoom updates continue after it. Fallback if depth still drops: a separate non-RoomPlan depth pass.

open_question_answers.question: Does chaining RoomPlan's internal ARSessionDelegate (multiplexer) work on iOS 18.3 without breaking tracking? cosmic-ios claims yes; Meta Ocean overwrites the delegate outright. Device test with a log of didUpdate counts.
open_question_answers.answer: Architecture answer: do not depend on chaining. ARSession.delegate is a single weak slot (`weak var delegate: (any ARSessionDelegate)?`) and Apple documents no RoomPlan-internal ARSessionDelegate. Meta's ocean sets arSession.delegate = self after run() with no multiplexer and still expects all RoomCaptureSessionDelegate callbacks. Set Mapper's own delegate on its own ARSession before RoomCaptureSession(arSession:). As a cheap guard, after captureSession(_:didStartWith:) check `session.arSession.delegate === mapperDelegate`; if RoomPlan replaced it, capture the existing delegate and install a forwarding multiplexer (forward every ARSessionDelegate/ARSessionObserver method, keep a strong reference to the captured one since the slot is weak). Needs device test: log per second the counts of session(_:didUpdate:) frames, captureSession(_:didUpdate:) room updates, and camera.trackingState, plus whether the preview renders, for both 'delegate set before run' and 'delegate set after run'.

open_question_answers.question: Exact USDZ node names (Wall_0_grp / WallN / Object_grp) are community-derived; if Mapper ever re-imports the USDZ, read the metadata dictionary instead of assuming names.
open_question_answers.answer: Agreed: Apple documents no USDZ prim/node naming scheme for CapturedRoom.export or CapturedStructure.export, only that the output is USD and (before iOS 17.4) the file name must not start with a digit. Mapper should treat the USDZ as an output-only interchange file. For its own data it should persist CapturedRoom / CapturedStructure via their Codable conformance (encode(to:) and init(from:), both documented) and rebuild geometry from surfaces/objects (dimensions, transform, category, identifier), never by parsing node names. If a USDZ is ever re-imported, map prims via the metadata file and treat names as best effort.

open_question_answers.question: The metadata file encoding: Apple describes it as an 'encoded dictionary of String to UUID' and samples use .plist; whether the extension selects plist vs JSON encoding is undocumented.
open_question_answers.answer: The current doc JSON only says metadataURL is 'A location that the captured room metadata exports to' (CapturedRoom and CapturedStructure export(to:metadataURL:modelProvider:exportOptions:), iOS 17.0+); no encoding or extension rule is documented, and CapturedRoom.Error includes urlMissingFileExtension, so an extension is required. Architecture: Mapper should not rely on this file as its store. Pass a .plist URL like Apple's samples, and make any reader sniff the format (PropertyListSerialization handles XML and binary plists; fall back to JSONSerialization). The source of truth remains the Codable CapturedRoom/CapturedStructure. Needs device test: export once with .plist and once with .json and log the first bytes (bplist00 vs '<?xml' vs '{') to learn whether the extension changes the encoding.

open_question_answers.question: No Apple figure for metric accuracy (cm); field tests vary from 1-5 cm to 37 cm drift on a 6.45 m wall. Decide whether Mapper needs a user-driven calibration/measurement correction step.
open_question_answers.answer: Apple publishes no centimeter accuracy figure for RoomPlan dimensions; its ML research page reports detection precision/recall (about 95 percent walls and windows, about 90 percent doors), not length error. Community and LiDAR studies put raw LiDAR at about 1 cm on close features and a few cm per room, with drift growing across long walls and multi-room scans. Architecture: yes, include an optional user-driven correction: let the user enter one known reference length (tape measure) per room or structure and apply a uniform scale factor to exported dimensions, show accuracy as a tolerance via the Units module, and record the correction in the project file so it is reversible. Needs device test: per docs/TEST_PLAN.md accuracy protocol, log RoomPlan wall.dimensions versus tape measurements for short (under 3 m) and long (over 6 m) walls, single-room and after StructureBuilder merge.

open_question_answers.question: Whether StructureBuilder accepts rooms scanned in separate app launches when each new ARSession relocalizes from a saved ARWorldMap (documented as supported, but exceedSceneSizeLimit reports exist).
open_question_answers.answer: Documented as supported: StructureBuilder.capturedStructure(from:) (iOS 17.0+, async throws) succeeds when all rooms share compatible world space, and the docs name two ways: reuse the same ARSession across RoomCaptureSessions (stop(pauseARSession: false)), or load a saved ARWorldMap into a new ARSession and wait until camera tracking goes from .limited(.relocalizing) to .normal before starting the next RoomCaptureSession(arSession:). The article says the same for app restarts and backgrounding. Architecture: after each room, save ARWorldMap (session.getCurrentWorldMap) plus the Codable CapturedRoom to disk; on resume, run ARWorldTrackingConfiguration with initialWorldMap, implement sessionShouldAttemptRelocalization returning true, gate the next room scan on tracking .normal, and show a 'return to last room' prompt. Handle both a thrown error from capturedStructure(from:) (incompatible space) and RoomCaptureSession.CaptureError.exceedSceneSizeLimit (scene grew past framework limits) by keeping per-room results and exporting rooms separately. Needs device test: scan room A, kill the app, relaunch, relocalize, scan room B, and log whether capturedStructure(from:) succeeds, its error, and the gap between shared wall positions.
